baseline_models.mechanism: The first-person deliberation treats lesser gods as deliberately acquired dependencies. Their claim to worship is tested as a protection apparatus: whether they can supply sufficiency and extraction when harm comes from the higher sovereign.

activation_trace.role: Making or acquiring something for oneself frames the gods as deliberately procured dependencies.
Otherness with lower rank places the acquired gods outside and beneath the primary relation.
What is made an object of worship is the candidate dependency being functionally tested.
Kifaya and substitution supply the test of whether another can adequately stand in for the vulnerable speaker.
Extraction from a predicament supplies the terminal protection function that the acquired gods lack.

changed_reading.before: The ayah simply rejects belief in other gods.
changed_reading.after: The ayah audits the act of procuring lower divine patrons and rejects them because the proposed protection system has no sufficiency or rescue capacity.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّى شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
baseline_models.mechanism: Intercession adds a helper to a needy party, but the ayah measures that addition twice: it yields no increment of sufficiency at all and cannot complete an extraction from danger. Numerical or social addition therefore creates no causal surplus.

activation_trace.role: Joining one thing to another supplies the additive structure whose effectiveness is being denied.
The intercessor joins the claimant by plea or aid, supplying the social mechanism of the proposed help.
Adequacy and standing in for another provide the first failed outcome of the added helper.
The most general object under negation reduces the helper's contribution to no identifiable effect.
Actual extraction from danger provides the second and terminal failed outcome.

changed_reading.after: The ayah dismantles the logic that adding patrons adds leverage: neither incremental adequacy nor final extraction appears.

baseline_models.mechanism: Merciful tenderness and harmful loss are deliberately held inside one conditional. Harm is not presented as an independent force opposed to mercy; it remains inside the Merciful's intention, while every rival blocking or rescue claim is removed.

activation_trace.role: Intention and purposive will supply the governing causal condition.
Tenderness and beneficence make the attribution of possible harm a live theological tension rather than a neutral power claim.
Loss, ill condition, and the opposite of benefit supply the feared outcome.
Rescue would require extraction from an outcome already located within the Merciful's will.

changed_reading.before: If God sends harm, idols cannot help.
changed_reading.after: Even feared harm lies within the Merciful's unshared agency, so mercy cannot be secured by outsourcing dependence to a rival rescuer.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the speaker rejects false rescuers and declares faith, the narrative passes abruptly to entry into the Garden, forgiveness, and honor, then says no heavenly army was sent after him. Successful rescue is therefore legible as secured destination and reception, not necessarily immunity from every intervening injury.

activation_trace.role: Extraction from a predicament anchors the focus question about what counts as rescue.
Entry into an interior supplies a successful passage and destination immediately after the speaker's declaration.
The sheltered garden supplies the destination into which the speaker is received.
Covering the fault and protecting its bearer from its effect supplies one dimension of the attained rescue.
Honor and noble reception supply the positive outcome beyond mere escape.
The explicitly unsent mutually supporting host removes military extraction as the mechanism of his successful outcome.

structural_cues: 36:25-27 places declaration, Garden entry, forgiveness, and honor in an uninterrupted sequence.
36:28 immediately denies that a heavenly army was sent after him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an abrupt transition but does not state the intervening event; I infer that the sequence redefines successful rescue by outcome. A live alternative is that the Garden scene is a visionary or proleptic reward without specifying bodily harm.

changed_reading.before: A true rescuer would prevent the speaker from undergoing harm.
changed_reading.after: The focus can reject false rescue without promising worldly immunity: the surah measures deliverance by final entry, forgiveness, and honor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus conditional is replayed as a maritime emergency: divine willing leads to drowning, no answering helper is available, and the exact rescue root is negated. The next ayah makes mercy the sole exception and describes the result as a time-bounded reprieve.

activation_trace.role: Merciful tenderness anchors the divine title whose relation to harm needs resolution.
Extraction from danger anchors the rescue function denied to the gods.
Willing related to an outcome supplies a context parallel to the focus's divine-intent conditional.
Drowning in water turns generic harm into a concrete predicament requiring extraction.
Aid that answers distress supplies the unavailable intermediate helper.
The repeated extraction root directly instantiates the focus's denied rescue.
Mercy itself supplies the sole stated exception to the no-rescue sequence.
Extended enjoyment supplies the bounded reprieve produced by mercy rather than an independent counterpower.

structural_cues: 36:43 repeats a divine-will conditional and ends with the same ن ق ذ rescue root as 36:23.
36:44 immediately introduces mercy as an exception and limits the reprieve to a time.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies willing, drowning, absent aid, negated rescue, and then mercy; I read the adjacent exception as identifying the only rescue source. The alternative is that mercy prevents drowning before extraction rather than rescuing after submersion.

changed_reading.before: The Merciful may harm while idols happen to be unable to rescue.
changed_reading.after: The later matched sequence identifies mercy itself as the only exception to non-rescue; idols fail because rescue is an act of the same sovereign, not a rival intervention.

context_deltas.mechanism: Parallel if-we-will clauses depict harm as alteration of the faculties and routes by which escape would occur: sight is erased, form and place are fixed, and going forward or returning becomes impossible. A rescuer inside the same order cannot restore an affordance that the governing will has removed.

activation_trace.role: Divine intention anchors the focus conditional later expanded by parallel willing clauses.
Loss and ill condition anchor the generic harm that later scenes render as disabled capacity.
Extraction anchors the need for a viable route or faculty through which rescue could operate.
Divine willing opens the first parallel conditional that specifies a mode of harm.
Loss of light and sight removes the perceptual capacity needed to find the path.
Repeated divine willing opens the second parallel conditional.
Transformation of created form supplies bodily alteration as another mode of harm.
Capacity and ability are explicitly negated, defining the practical result of transformation.
Passing onward supplies the forward route that has become unavailable.
Returning supplies the reverse route that is also unavailable.

structural_cues: 36:66-67 repeats the same willing protasis while varying the disabled faculty.
The two outcomes cover perception, bodily state, forward motion, and return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel conditionals and removed faculties; I treat them as concrete specifications of the focus's generic harm and as an explanation of failed rescue. The live alternative is that 36:23's harm is narrower and need not imply comprehensive capacity erasure.

changed_reading.before: Harm is an adverse event from which a sufficiently strong helper might extract someone.
changed_reading.after: Harm can be the sovereign removal of sight, form, capacity, and route itself, leaving no independent operational channel for a lower helper.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later judgment sequence says no self is wronged in any respect, limits recompense to intentional work, and makes bodily members witnesses to what was acquired. This bounds the focus's mercy-harm tension by accountable consequence and weakens any model of intercession as a way to bypass the evidentiary relation between deed and outcome.

activation_trace.role: Merciful tenderness anchors the apparent tension with harmful consequence.
Loss and ill condition anchor the outcome whose moral direction the context qualifies.
Pleading aid for another anchors the possible attempt to alter the relation between conduct and consequence.
The general object under negated wrong excludes even an identifiable unit of injustice.
Matching an act with its recompense supplies the directional relation between deed and outcome.
Intentional action supplies the accountable input to recompense.
Testimony that discloses by knowledge supplies evidence independent of a self-serving plea.
Acquiring gain supplies the acquisition vocabulary for deeds attributed to the person.

structural_cues: 36:54 negates wrong to any self and restricts recompense to what people were doing.
36:65 seals mouths and relocates speech and testimony to the body's own members.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-wrong, act-matched recompense, and embodied evidence; I infer that at least judicial harm is morally bounded and not open to patronage override. The alternative is that the focus conditional primarily concerns nonpunitive worldly adversity.

changed_reading.before: The phrase about the Merciful intending harm risks sounding like arbitrary adversity that a patron might negotiate away.
changed_reading.after: Within the surah's judgment frame, harmful consequence is bounded by non-wrong and evidenced action, so intercession cannot function as a patronage bypass.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first presents created cattle as legitimately owned, made usable, and productive of benefits; it then repeats the focus's act of taking lower gods in hope of support. Their incapacity and the ambiguous mustered-army relation expose a category error: worshippers procure divine patrons as utility assets, but the expected provider-client relation either reverses or collapses into a useless assembled force.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition for oneself anchors the focus as a deliberate patronage arrangement.
Useful adequacy anchors the expected service that the acquired patrons fail to provide.
Aid by joining another's cause supplies the patron-client service being sought.
Ownership and disposal supply the legitimate asset relation that precedes the false divine acquisition.
Benefit as the opposite of harm supplies the real utility produced by the created animals.
The repeated acquisition verb makes the focus's individual deliberation a whole-community practice.
Otherness and lower rank repeat the focus's placement of the acquired gods.
The worship and worshipped branch resolves both the primary divine reference and the acquired deities in the repeated contrast.
Support and making another prevail state the hoped-for return on acquiring gods.
Capacity is explicitly denied to the proposed patrons.
The repeated support branch names the exact service they cannot perform.
A mutually supporting host supplies the collective relation that replaces the expected individual rescue.
Being brought into presence supplies the mustered or presented condition of that host.

structural_cues: 36:71-73 moves through creation, ownership, usability, benefit, and gratitude before 36:74 turns to acquiring gods.
36:74 repeats the focus phrase and states hoped-for support; 36:75 immediately denies capacity and support.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the utility sequence, repeated acquisition, failed support, and a pronoun-dense army clause; I infer a critique of treating worship as asset procurement and keep a patron-client reversal live. The alternative is that the gods themselves, rather than their worshippers, are the useless army brought for them.

changed_reading.before: Taking gods is an abstract doctrinal mistake about how many deities exist.
changed_reading.after: Taking gods is a failed utility and patronage strategy: unlike genuinely beneficial created assets, the acquired patrons cannot serve and may instead conscript or merely encumber their clients.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah places every thing in an exhaustive record, then closes with an intended thing passing through divine speech into occurrence and every thing under sovereignty and return. The focus's negated anything is therefore not only a minimizer; it denies intercession an unrecorded object, causal interval, or residual jurisdiction.

activation_trace.role: The general knowable object anchors the zero contribution asserted of intercession.
Adequacy and substitution define the operative share denied with respect to any thing.
Totality and enclosure extend the record without remainder.
Every knowable object becomes an item within the exhaustive record.
Counting by exhaustive enumeration supplies the recording mechanism.
Intention selects a thing as the object of efficacious will.
The intended knowable object repeats the focus's thing vocabulary at the point of realization.
Uttered speech supplies the expressed link between intention and occurrence.
Occurrence and presence in time supply both the imperative endpoint and realized state.
Sovereignty supplies the comprehensive jurisdiction containing every thing.
Totality again removes any remainder outside that jurisdiction.
Every knowable object is explicitly placed under the closing sovereignty claim.
Return supplies the terminal movement back to the same sovereign.

structural_cues: 36:12 combines every thing with exhaustive enumeration.
36:82-83 moves from intending a thing to its occurrence, then to sovereignty over every thing and universal return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated thing lexeme across record, will, occurrence, sovereignty, and return; I infer a continuous jurisdiction that leaves no operational remainder for intercession. The alternative is that the focus's شيء remains only an idiomatic minimizer without deliberate linkage to the later recurrences.

changed_reading.before: Not anything merely intensifies the statement that intercession helps very little or not at all.
changed_reading.after: Not anything denies a residual domain in which intercession could operate: every object is already enumerated, intended into occurrence, held under sovereignty, and returned.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The comparison is surprising because 36:14 concerns reinforcement of messengers, not cultic intercession. It remains anchored through the focus branch of adding one to another and a whole-surah two-plus-third reinforcement pattern, but downstream prose should present it as a structural analogy about authorized addition, not as lexical equivalence.

activation_trace.role: Adding one thing to another supplies the focus's latent numerical structure.
Joining one to one and making two supplies an explicit authorized pairing.
Reinforcement and strengthening state that the authorized addition has real force.
A completing third supplies the added member through whom reinforcement occurs.

changed_reading.before: Adding another figure is either always useful or always useless.
changed_reading.after: The surah distinguishes sender-authorized reinforcement, which can strengthen a mission, from self-procured divine multiplication, which creates no intercessory leverage.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation is surprising and form-distant because the actual focus verb belongs to intending, while the packet's split mapping also exposes the semantic field of repelling and preventing. It remains anchored to the supplied mapped inventory and the focus's explicit rescue test, but downstream prose must not translate يُرِدْ as repel; it may mention only a secondary warding-off shadow around the security logic.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant mapped branch of repelling and preventing supplies a root-distant shadow of warding harm off.
Loss and ill condition provide the object that a security system would attempt to ward off.
Extraction from danger keeps the distant branch tied to the focus's explicit protection test.

changed_reading.before: The clause tests only whether gods can react after divinely intended harm.
changed_reading.after: At the edge of the split inventory, it also shadows the broader failure of secondary security: neither warding the harm off nor extracting the sufferer belongs to the acquired gods.

strongest_changes: 36:43-44 turns the hypothetical no-rescue claim into willing, drowning, absent aid, and repeated non-rescue, then names mercy as the sole exception.
36:71-75 exposes taking gods as failed utility acquisition and leaves the expected patron-client relation reversed or collapsed into a useless mustered force.
36:12 and 36:82-83 place every thing across exhaustive record, efficacious intention, sovereignty, and return, leaving no residual domain for intercession.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context supplied more than doctrinal repetition: it supplied matched conditional syntax, the exact rescue root, a mercy exception, a creation-ownership-benefit contrast, disabled escape capacities, and a closing will-to-being chain.
remaining_uncertainties: The pronoun relations in 36:75 allow either worshippers serving the gods or the gods appearing as a useless army for the worshippers.
The transition at 36:26-27 supports outcome-based rescue but does not itself state what intervened between the declaration and Garden entry.
The authorized-reinforcement analogy and the non-dominant ر د د mapping should remain explicitly exploratory rather than control the primary reading.
The focus's harm may include worldly adversity as well as judicial consequence, so 36:54 should qualify rather than exhaust its scope.
